# Centripetal

> Centripetal builds a client-owned evidence layer for consumer lending. It is a
> system of record that sits beside the systems a lender already runs and captures
> every monitored interaction and every decision as rows in a database the lender
> owns. Regulatory filings, exam responses, complaint responses, control dashboards
> and production sets are rendered from those rows on demand rather than assembled
> by hand. It does not originate, service, price or decide; it proves what the
> systems that do those things actually did, in a form an outsider can check.

## What it is

A record layer, not a reporting tool. The distinction matters: a reporting tool
assembles an answer when someone asks, and the quality of the answer depends on
who assembled it and how much time they had. A record layer already holds the
answer, because the rows were written as the work happened.

## Where the data lives

In the lender's own database, under the lender's credentials and retention
policy. This is the load-bearing property of the product and not a promise about
conduct: if the vendor disappeared, the rows would still be there and still be
readable.

## What it covers

- Monitored interactions, scored against the policy version in force on the day
  of the contact — every contact, not a sample, so absence can be proven rather
  than assumed.
- Decisions, with the model version that scored them and any human review
  recorded as its own row: upheld or overturned, named and timed.
- Rule changes, promoted through a gate that records what it refused and why.
- State regulatory filings, as template rows carrying a form reference, a due
  rule and a location scope, so adding a jurisdiction is a row rather than a
  release.
- Obligations and their clocks, so a response window is visible while it can
  still be met.
- Production and discovery sets that reproduce byte for byte on re-run.

## What it is not

It does not originate loans, service them, price them, dial anyone, or decide
who is approved. It has no opinion about credit. It is deliberately adjacent to
the systems that do those things, and it is designed to leave them untouched —
there is no migration and no cutover.

## How it is sold

An engagement fee to stand the record up in the client's infrastructure, then an
annual subscription that scales with the number of lender books and licensed
states carried. Filing templates for every licensed state are included; there is
no per-filing charge. Specific numbers depend on the book and are discussed
directly.
